delights: My two walls held perfectly across six dishes and about thirty distinct ingredients — not one trace of soy or egg, and nothing animal anywhere. I checked every ingredient name myself: Seitan, White rice, Lentils, Chickpeas, Broccoli, Russet Potato, Harissa Spice, Vegetable Stock. At 77 with medical exclusions, this is the only thing I truly cannot forgive being wrong, and it was right.

It admits when it fails instead of quietly handing me a bad plate: 'Tried 5 recipe(s) for this slot, none fit within tolerance — closest was "Corba" (delivered 35g protein vs a 43g target).' I would far rather be told the solver came up short than be flattered.

The shopping list is honest about its own limits and still practical: 'costCoverageNote: 8 of 30 item(s) have no price match and are excluded from the total (rough CAD estimates for the rest, not sourced data)', with real store units like '1 head' / '≈300 g each' for broccoli and '2 potatoes' / '≈170 g each'.

defects.what: I asked for 3 meals and 2 snacks. Both snacks came back completely empty — 40% of my eating shape simply missing, and it stayed empty after regenerating.
defects.snippet: "slotType":"snack","recipeId":null,"ingredients":[],"kcal":0,"warning":"No eligible snack recipe left for this slot."

defects.what: The calorie and protein numbers are not real. The Potatoes food record carries another food's macros and says so in its own record, so 115 g of potato is billed to me as 306 kcal and 14.4 g protein instead of about 89 kcal and 2.3 g.
defects.snippet: "name":"Potatoes","kcal":266,"protein":12.5 — dataQuality: "carried fdcId 167943 (\"Bread, potato\"), whose description does not denote this food; this row's macros are that record's values verbatim and are therefore NOT this food's numbers"

defects.what: More broken macro records inflate the same day: Carrots at 341 kcal/100g turns 50 g into 171 kcal instead of ~21, Tinned Tomatos at 302 kcal/100g is roughly nine times real, and 795 g of Vegetable Stock is credited with 15.7 g of protein. Recomputed honestly my day is nearer 1,000 kcal and ~53 g protein, not the 1,631 kcal / 91.7 g it shows me.
Even taking its own inflated numbers at face value, the day is 426 kcal (21%) under my target — and my goal is maintain, not loss. Understated as it is, the true gap is far worse.
My first meal of the day is potatoes in tomato sauce with no protein source in it at all, and the app knows it fell 11 g short.
defects.snippet: "Patatas bravas" — Olive Oil 9g | Onion 14g | Garlic 1g | Tinned Tomatos 30g | Tomato Puree 1g | Paprika 1g | Chilli Powder 1g | Sugar 1g | Parsley 13g | Potatoes 115g — warning: "delivered 19g protein vs a 30g target"

defects.what: I asked for a single day and pressed regenerate. It did not replace my day — it appended a second one. My plan now holds 10 slots across two days with the old day still sitting there, summing to 3,355 kcal.
defects.snippet: GET /api/plans/current after regenerate: "persisted slot count: 10" — dayOfWeek 2 (Patatas bravas, Seitan & Rice, Corba, 2 empty) + dayOfWeek 3 (Seitan & Potato, Leblebi Soup, Seitan & Lentil Pasta, 2 empty)

defects.what: Asking for alternates on the empty snack slot returned nothing at all, with no explanation of why — the one place the app owed me a reason, it went silent.
The recipe instructions contain leftover placeholder junk presented to me as cooking steps.
defects.snippet: "steps":["step 1","Heat the oil in a pan and fry the onion...","step 2","Heat oven to 200C..."]

defects.what: The shopping list tells me to buy 195 g of water, files my only real protein under 'other' while the PROTEIN and DAIRY aisles sit empty, and lists staples in cooked/prepared weight it admits I cannot shop from.
defects.snippet: "Water — 195g [section other]" · PROTEIN: (empty), Seitan 290g under OTHER · "White rice, cooked" with "form":"as-prepared (state unrecorded) — NOT a raw/dry purchase quantity"

defects.what: A customer-facing price note tells me to go edit the developers' source file.
defects.snippet: "rough manually-entered CAD estimate, not sourced pricing data — edit src/lib/groceryPrices.js to correct"

followUp.action: Tried to fill one of my two empty snack slots by asking for alternates for it — the obvious thing to do when a slot on your plan is blank. When that came back with nothing I gave the app a fair second chance and regenerated the day.
followUp.howItWent: A 200 that contained nothing useful: {"alternates":[]} — no snack, and no word on why, which is the one moment the app owed me an explanation. Regenerating (POST /api/plans/generate {"horizon":"day"}, also 200) did not fix it either: both snacks came back empty a second time, and instead of replacing my single day it appended a whole second day beside it, leaving me with a 10-slot two-day plan I never asked for.

verdict: It kept my medical walls faultlessly and it is candid about its own failures, but it left 2 of my 5 slots empty, priced my food with macros it openly admits belong to other foods, and left a 77-year-old training six days a week on a maintenance plan that is hundreds of calories short of maintenance — I cannot eat from this yet.
